extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians writing research papers (researchers and graduate students)
extracted.subtask_description: Advice for composing clear, modern mathematical research papers (titles, abstracts, introductions, references, micro-style, LaTeX usage, and promotion) that are readable online and by non-native English speakers. Emphasizes organization, precise citation, screen-friendly formatting, and dissemination practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Golden rule: Be clear
rubrics_metrics.description: "Be clear!" — the single rule that subsumes the others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear writing is the primary and overriding goal; clarity is the sustainable competitive advantage in situations where many groups pursue the same theorem. All other tips serve this goal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title: informative and searchable
rubrics_metrics.description: Title should be informative, searchable, and avoid clever puns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optimize titles for discoverability (search engines, arXiv). Prefer plain, descriptive phrasing over witticisms that harm searchability or clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract: self-contained and notation-free
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstract must be self-contained, assume no notation, state the main theorem(s) in plain words, and be ≤ 200 words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write the abstract so it conveys the main results to a reader who won't scan the paper; keep it short and avoid symbols or unexplained terminology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduction: include six sub-sections
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduction should contain: context and motivation; statement of main results; comparison to prior work; outline of methods; structure of the paper; acknowledgments and conventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the introduction to tell the full narrative: why the problem matters, what you prove, how it relates to existing work, how you achieve it, and how the paper is organized. Include technical conventions (notation, assumptions) and acknowledgments here or reference them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table of contents for long papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a table of contents for any paper longer than ~30 pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps navigation when readers access the paper in pieces; especially useful for screen reading and long expositions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreword / final remarks: connect to broader narrative
rubrics_metrics.description: Include final remarks or a foreword to connect results to broader narrative and indicate future directions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use closing sections to situate the work, suggest open problems, and guide further reading or follow-up work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgments: list funding and helpful conversations
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge every funding source and every helpful conversation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be thorough and precise in acknowledgments; this is part of scholarly practice and credit allocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite all relevant prior work
rubrics_metrics.description: Cite every relevant prior work, including work that your result supersedes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comprehensive citation practices avoid misattribution and help readers trace the literature. Do not omit earlier or related contributions even if superseded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite original sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Cite the original source of results/ideas rather than only textbook copies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer primary sources to secondary references so credit goes to originators and readers can find the most accurate account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite preprints with arXiv IDs
rubrics_metrics.description: When citing preprints, include arXiv IDs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide stable and direct links to preprints; arXiv IDs improve discoverability and allow readers to access the cited material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Place citations precisely at claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Place citations precisely at the claim being supported rather than vaguely in a paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite specific statements to avoid ambiguity about what the reference supports; precise placement improves reader trust and verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose a consistent citation format
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt a consistent reference format (Pak prefers numeric, alphabetical-by-author).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistency in citation style improves readability; pick a system and apply it uniformly across the paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-cite within the paper
rubrics_metrics.description: Refer back to your earlier numbered claims and cross-cite within the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use internal cross-references to help readers navigate dependencies between claims, lemmas, and sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Master grammar, syntax, and punctuation
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure correct grammar, syntax, and punctuation; copyedit professionally if necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No excuses for language errors—even for non-native speakers. Professional copyediting improves clarity and perceived quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid pedantic phrasing
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid pedantic language; prefer direct, simple forms (e.g., replace 'We may write without loss of generality' with 'Assume').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trim unnecessary verbosity and hedging that obscures meaning; be direct and concrete when stating assumptions and results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplify writing style
rubrics_metrics.description: Use short sentences, plain words, and active voice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simple prose aids comprehension, especially for non-native English readers and for readers skimming on screens. Favor clarity over rhetorical flourish.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use LaTeX carefully
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not blindly trust LaTeX auto-formatting; check spacing, hyphenation, and line breaks by eye.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proofread the typeset output for awkward breaks, equation placement, and formatting issues; fix manual spacing and punctuation around math as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figures and illustrations should be self-contained and meaningful
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures can replace paragraphs; design captions to be self-contained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use well-designed figures to convey ideas succinctly; captions should explain the figure without requiring the reader to hunt through the text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optimize titles and abstracts for online discovery
rubrics_metrics.description: Because the paper is online, make titles and abstracts searchable and discoverable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use keywords and plain phrasing that search engines and readers will use; think about how readers find your paper via web searches or arXiv.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format for screen reading
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers are often read on screens; use displayed equations sparingly and avoid long inline runs that break on small screens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arrange equations and paragraphs to be readable on various devices; avoid layouts that require wide horizontal space or cause awkward wrapping on phones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write to win credit in competitive environments
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple groups may race to the same theorem; clear writing helps secure credit and resolve attribution disputes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about what is new and whose work you're building on; clarity can determine recognition in fast-moving fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make sections independently readable
rubrics_metrics.description: Readers access papers in pieces, so sections should be independently readable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each section should contain enough context to be understood in isolation (e.g., when readers jump to a specific theorem or proof). Use local reminders of notation and assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use hyperlinks and active citation links
rubrics_metrics.description: Because the paper has hyperlinks, use ull cross-references (e.g., \cref) and make citations active links; include arXiv URLs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make navigation frictionless by linking to referenced sections and external resources; this is particularly useful in online reading and cross-referencing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write simply for non-native English readers
rubrics_metrics.description: Many readers are graduate students for whom English is a second language; simplicity is mercy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer plain vocabulary, avoid idioms and dense sentences, and keep sentence structure straightforward to aid international readership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing is necessary but not sufficient for impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Good writing alone won't ensure attention; dissemination matters too.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine clear writing with active promotion to maximize reach and recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post preprints to arXiv before journal acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: Post your paper to arXiv prior to journal acceptance to ensure timely discoverability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early arXiv posting helps establish precedence, increases visibility, and facilitates community feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Present at conferences and engage on MathOverflow
rubrics_metrics.description: Present results at conferences and be active on MathOverflow to promote your work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oral and online engagement complement written exposition and help disseminate results to interested communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow up with expository writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Write a blog post or expository note to accompany the research paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expository pieces translate technical results for a broader audience and can attract readers who might not read the research paper directly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain a clean personal website
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep a tidy personal website that lists and links to your papers and preprints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A clear, up-to-date personal page helps readers find your work and contact information; it is part of professional online presence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan rewrites and update preprints: writing is never finished
rubrics_metrics.description: "Writing is never finished, only abandoned." Plan rewrites and update preprints; treat the paper as a living object.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Iteratively improve exposition, correct errors, and update versions on arXiv or your website as the work and community feedback evolve.
